title: Sort and Count Shapes Worksheets for Kindergarten
intro: Teach sorting by one named shape attribute at a time.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Read the target shape name and discuss its sides and corners. Have the student mark each matching shape, then count the marked group.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

A collection might contain two circles, three triangles, and four squares. If the question asks for triangles, circle the three triangles and write 3. The circles and squares stay on the page, but they do not belong to the category being counted.

First name the kind of shape. Next mark every matching picture. Finally count only the marked pictures. Separating these actions helps a child keep track of both the sorting rule and the number.

Ask your student

What makes this shape belong in our group?

If your student needs help

If color or size distracts the student, compare differently colored examples of the same shape.
